name: German nationalism in Austria
summary: Austrian German nationalism (Deutschnationalismus) holds that German-speaking Austrians belong to the German nation and should be united with Germany in a Greater Germany rather than form a separate Austrian nation or live in the multi-ethnic Habsburg empire. Historically, under Georg von Schönerer, it combined pan-Germanism with antisemitism, anti-Slavism, anti-clericalism (Away from Rome) and hostility to the Habsburgs and political Catholicism. After 1945 the Third Camp, the VdU and then the FPÖ, kept a German cultural identity while accepting Austrian statehood, together with strong stress on immigration limits, family and sovereignty.
scope: The profile represents the Austrian Third Camp tradition as a whole: the Schönerer era and Linz Program (1882, 1885 Aryan paragraph), the interwar pan-German parties up to the 1938 Anschluss, and the post-1945 German-national wing of the FPÖ as documented in its 2011 programme. Where the eras differ, such as on democracy, antisemitism, and Anschluss, the answer is lowered in confidence or set to neutral. It excludes Austrian nationalism, Austrofascism, German nationalism in Germany, and Nazism as a distinct movement.

universal-healthcare.rationale: The FPÖ programme wants a public health service giving everyone the best prevention and care and rejects multi-class medicine, so a nationalist adherent backs state-guaranteed care, especially for citizens.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: The programme speaks of fair wages but names no minimum-wage policy; support is inferred from its pro-worker 'social homeland' language.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: The movement was split: modern Third Camp programmes endorse a market economy, but Schönerer attacked liberal business dealings and backed nationalising a railway, so adherents do not simply trust markets over government.

public-ownership.rationale: Schönerer supported nationalising the Nordbahn railway, the only documented public-ownership position; extending it to energy and utilities is an inference.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: The FPÖ programme demands low taxes, treats labour income and capital income as equally valuable and favours burden relief over redistribution.

unions-good.rationale: The sources discuss courting workers on a national basis but give no stance on unions as such, and adherents split between nationalist labour organising and business-friendly Mittelstand politics.

property-fundamental.rationale: The programme lists protection of private property among its guiding principles, though not as an overriding absolute right.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Schönerer attacked 'Jewish' capital and the programme criticises monopolistic agribusiness and media monopolies, implying support for curbs on concentrated corporate power.

cut-welfare.rationale: The programme affirms a social state protecting against old age, illness and unemployment while demanding action against welfare abuse, so adherents want welfare policed rather than cut.

worker-ownership.rationale: The programme favours individual property formation and small business over collective ownership; no source discusses worker-owned firms.

surveillance-ok.rationale: The programme tells the state to use all its means against terrorism and organised crime; surveillance is inferred from that security emphasis.

legalize-drugs.rationale: The programme commits to fighting addiction and the drug trade and gives no support for legalisation.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: The programme stresses free speech as a basic liberty and the movement historically resisted speech limits, though post-war Austrian law restricts Nazi speech.

strong-leader.rationale: Schönerer was given the title Führer by followers and showed authoritarian leanings, but the modern programme is formally democratic, so support is moderate and inferred.

state-harmful.rationale: A nationalism built on the nation-state and a Rechtsstaat programme cannot see the state as harmful; it wants a stronger, self-determined state.

limit-guns.rationale: The programme stresses citizens' self-defence and a strong security apparatus but never mentions gun law; opposition to strict limits is inferred.

empower-police-military.rationale: The programme demands the best possible training and equipment for the security forces and the Bundesheer.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: The family-centred, order-focused programme gives no support; opposition is inferred from its traditional social outlook.

decide-locally.rationale: The Linz Program opposed extending federalism within Austria and wanted German centralised unity, although the modern programme invokes subsidiarity.

rehabilitation.rationale: The programme puts protection of society and crime victims first and says resocialisation must respect that priority.

traditional-family.rationale: The programme calls the family of man, woman and children the natural nucleus of society and ranks marriage of man and woman above other unions.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: The programme explicitly rejects even a separate legal institution for same-sex couples and reserves the privileged status to marriage between man and woman.

abortion-legal.rationale: The programme speaks of the protection of life and of human life being beyond utility considerations, pointing against broad legal abortion.

more-religion-public.rationale: Schönerer led the anti-clerical Away from Rome movement and the FPÖ programme wants church-state separation, treating Christianity only as a cultural heritage.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Racial nationalism marked Schönerer's movement and the programme rejects preferential treatment to offset disadvantages.

gender-social-construct.rationale: The programme rejects gender mainstreaming and affirms a man-woman family model.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: The programme says language, history and culture of Austria are German and pledges protection of the mother tongue and traditions as its core identity commitment.

gradual-change.rationale: The movement was radical and agitational under Schönerer yet defended inherited tradition in its later form, so adherents are genuinely split.

reduce-immigration.rationale: The programme states flatly that Austria is not an immigration country and links citizenship to German language and cultural rooting.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: The programme demands sovereignty and a Europe of fatherlands, accepting UN mandates only for peacekeeping and humanitarian missions.

free-trade.rationale: The programme criticises globalisation and prizes national interest; the Linz Program's customs union with Germany was a bloc not free trade.

nation-first.rationale: The programme's title is Austria First and it demands that international commitments never disadvantage the Austrian population.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: The programme allows soldiers abroad only voluntarily, under UN mandate, for disaster relief, humanitarian tasks and peacekeeping, not armed intervention.

open-borders.rationale: The programme opposes mass immigration and defines the national community by language and culture, which excludes open borders.

limit-growth.rationale: The programme values environment but also growth for small business and export industry; degrowth is not a position it takes.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Climate is not addressed in the programme beyond environmental protection and rejection of nuclear power; drastic state action is inferred as unwelcome.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: The programme values technology and research but sets ethical limits and an idealist worldview; there is no stated faith in tech solving humanity's problems.

expand-nuclear.rationale: The programme states that Austria rejects the use of nuclear power for energy.

revolution-justified.rationale: The programme honours the 1848 revolution as a struggle for freedom while the movement used putsches against the republic, so adherents are split.

experts-over-public.rationale: The programme demands expanded direct democracy and referendums, giving the public the last word.

central-planning.rationale: The programme endorses a market economy and balanced budgets; central planning has no place.

socialized-markets.rationale: Only private small-business market capitalism is endorsed; the idea is never discussed.

land-value-tax.rationale: The programme wants low, simple taxes and protects property; a single land tax is never discussed.

tax-inheritance.rationale: The programme favours property formation and wealth passing within families, so heavy inheritance taxes are inferred as opposed.

basic-income.rationale: The programme ties welfare to effort and fights welfare abuse, which sits against an unconditional income.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: The Linz Program wanted a customs union with Germany to bind Austria economically to the Reich, and the movement favoured national economic interest.

state-directs-investment.rationale: The programme speaks of an economic policy free of ideological reservations and market-led growth, not planned strategic investment.

widespread-small-property.rationale: The programme promotes property formation, small and medium firms and a healthy peasantry freed from agribusiness interests.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: The programme is committed to market economy and wage-based performance reward.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Nothing in the sources addresses monetary regime; abolition is inferred as outside the programme's stability-oriented budget outlook.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: Schönerer's popular solidarism hints at national class cooperation but no source describes state-recognised wage bodies.

one-party-rule.rationale: The programme commits to democracy, proportional voting and separation of powers, though the movement was absorbed into the Nazi one-party state.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Schönerer remained hostile to the Habsburg monarchy even during the First World War and the movement favoured a republic joined to Germany.

democracy-best.rationale: The modern programme commits to democracy and the Rechtsstaat, and the 1918 German Austria republic was a democratic project, although historical adherents were ambivalent.

direct-votes.rationale: The programme demands expanded direct democracy and binding referendums on changes to treaties.

workers-councils.rationale: The programme wants parliamentary democracy with proportional elections; councils as a basis of power are contrary.

right-to-secede.rationale: German nationalists favoured detaching German regions into a larger state and the programme backs South Tyrol's self-determination, but a general right is not stated.

natural-rulers.rationale: Schönerer's Führer principle and völkisch hierarchy imply natural leadership, though the modern programme does not state it.

political-violence-never.rationale: Nationalist wings staged putsches in the 1930s and the movement was agitational, though the modern programme condemns extremism.

war-builds-character.rationale: The sources describe pan-German ethnocentrism but nothing on war as character-building; adherents are split.

separate-church-state.rationale: The programme explicitly grounds European culture on separation of church and state, and Schönerer's movement was anti-clerical.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Anti-clerical heritage and a programme built on constitutional law and separation reject scripture-based law.

private-courts-defense.rationale: The programme demands a strong state Rechtsstaat and army, never privatised justice or defence.

military-superiority.rationale: The programme wants self-defence capability and neutrality, not superiority over rivals.

ethnic-nation.rationale: The movement defined the nation by German ethnicity and language and demanded a state for all ethnic Germans.

class-struggle-history.rationale: The movement held that nation, not class, is the unit of politics; the Linz framers called their camp national, not liberal or clerical.

equal-outcomes.rationale: The programme says honest performance must pay and rejects levelling.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: The programme recognises autochthonous minorities as integrated members of the state, not as holders of separate land authority.

colonial-reparations.rationale: No source addresses it; the programme's sovereignty and 'help to self-help' attitude suggests opposition.

civilizational-union.rationale: The programme seeks a Europe of fatherlands and rejects the EU as political project, rather than uniting nations by shared civilisation.

self-interest-moral.rationale: The programme puts duties of solidarity with compatriots first, though it also values individual responsibility.

duties-before-rights.rationale: The programme lists citizens' duties of solidarity with compatriots, service and contributions as part of civic status.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: The programme speaks of animals as fellow creatures and biodiversity; intrinsic value is inferred.

limit-population.rationale: The programme demands birth-oriented family policy, the opposite of limiting population.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: The programme celebrates industry, technology and export strength.

accelerate-technology.rationale: The programme sets ethical limits on research and seeks to defend tradition.

human-enhancement.rationale: Ethical limits on research and rejection of misuse of gene technology make enhancement unwelcome.

algorithmic-government.rationale: The programme places sovereignty with citizens and direct votes; algorithmic rule is inferred as unwelcome.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: The security-first stance suggests state access over absolute privacy, but encryption is never discussed.

restore-past-order.rationale: The programme speaks of defending an inherited image of man and society, but progress is also welcomed.

results-over-ideology.rationale: The programme calls for economic policy free from ideological reservations and oriented on concrete challenges.

direct-action.rationale: The programme channels change through democratic procedures and direct votes, though the earlier movement used agitation.

means-match-ends.rationale: Not addressed in any source; adherents are indifferent.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Nothing in the sources approaches this; a modernising nationalist programme would reject it.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: The programme values specialised industry and dual vocational training.

distribute-by-need.rationale: The programme says performance must be rewarded and welfare reserved first for those who built prosperity.

production-for-use.rationale: The programme endorses market competition and profit-oriented enterprise.

profit-exploitation.rationale: The programme calls labour and capital income equally valuable, though Schönerer blamed 'Jewish' capitalists for exploitation, so a nationalist rather than Marxist version is held.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: The programme demands equal suffrage and rule of law.

collective-farming.rationale: The programme champions a healthy independent peasantry.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: The movement blamed nation-state conflicts, not capitalism, for war.

taxation-theft.rationale: The programme wants low taxes but affirms taxes to fund the social state and security.

harm-principle.rationale: The programme limits individual freedom by solidarity with the community and cultural values.

individual-rights-only.rationale: The movement defined rights by membership in the Volk, and the programme speaks of citizens' special rights and duties.

conscription.rationale: The programme explicitly endorses universal service duty for men in military or substitute service.

exit-over-voice.rationale: The programme prizes voting and direct democracy over emigration.

state-as-business.rationale: The programme speaks of a community of citizens with duties, not customers.

positive-liberty.rationale: The programme says freedom is not limited to material needs and promises social protection against hardship.

media-academia-power.rationale: The programme warns against monopolies and manipulation of public opinion in media and ideological interference in science.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Racial antisemitism and racial ethnocentrism marked the movement, though the modern programme avoids racial claims.

organic-representation.rationale: The programme endorses party-based proportional elections.

total-state.rationale: The programme affirms Rechtsstaat, liberal freedoms and limits on the state.

national-rebirth.rationale: Schönerer's Bismarck cult and irredentism imply national renewal, though decadence rhetoric is not documented.

territorial-expansion.rationale: The movement's historical aim was to absorb Austria into a Greater Germany, a union rather than conquest.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: The programme bases authority on democratic constitutional order.

bound-labor.rationale: The programme supports free citizens and equal rights.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: The programme says science serves truth-finding and rejects ideological interference.

universal-morality.rationale: The programme grounds its worldview in idealist, humanist values and the dignity of man.

single-common-good.rationale: The völkisch outlook sees one national community, and the programme stresses solidarity and common good.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Schönerer's antisemitism opposed Jews in public life and the sources do not mention Zionism, while modern FPÖ figures differ.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: The programme advocates for Altösterreicher of German mother tongue and expelled Heimatvertriebene.

revive-national-language.rationale: German is already the state language; the question does not apply.

workplace-democracy.rationale: The programme speaks of entrepreneurship and market economy, not co-determination.

school-vouchers.rationale: The programme assigns schooling to a state educational policy.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: The programme demands a state budget balanced over the economic cycle.

economic-freedom.rationale: The programme combines freedom as the highest good with market economy and private property.

rule-by-example.rationale: The programme relies on Rechtsstaat and law enforcement.

national-self-determination.rationale: The republic of German Austria was proclaimed in 1918 on self-determination grounds and the programme still invokes the Selbstbestimmungsrecht of peoples.

force-without-un.rationale: The programme limits foreign deployments to UN-mandated or humanitarian missions.

reason-over-faith.rationale: The programme calls its worldview idealist and not limited to material needs and values cultural-Christian heritage.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: The programme says prosperity must go first to those who earned it and social housing serves citizens.

work-for-welfare.rationale: The programme demands fighting welfare abuse and encouraging performance.

class-collaboration.rationale: The programme stresses a solidarity community and Schönerer's popular solidarism sought national class cooperation.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: The programme stresses preservation of cultural monuments and heritage.

dominated-front.rationale: The programme demands sovereignty but not a bloc against the West.

workers-nation.rationale: Schönerer's social reform plan was on a German-national basis and he courted workers via solidarism.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: The programme demands equal opportunity of men and women yet favours the family model; it does not call for law differentiating roles.

ban-interest.rationale: The programme endorses market economy; Schönerer's antisemitic attacks on finance did not extend to interest bans in the sources.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Schönerer demanded removal of Jews from public life and barred Jewish relatives from membership, though a segregation law is not documented.

state-class-instrument.rationale: The movement rejected class analysis; the nation is its community.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Energy supply is not addressed beyond rejecting nuclear power.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: The programme grants citizenship to those who master German, recognise values and are culturally rooted.

elite-replacement.rationale: Contemporary FPÖ-wing writers differ; the sources do not document the replacement theory in the programme.

proportional-representation.rationale: The programme explicitly demands an equal, direct proportional electoral system.

national-mission.rationale: Schuschnigg's 'better German state' claim and Austrian German-cultural mission imply a special role, though not spreading its constitution.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: The programme rejects quotas, gender mainstreaming and statistical inequality claims.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: The programme says life and dignity are not subject to utility considerations and warns against misuse of medicine and genetics.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: The programme stresses strengthening security forces; accountability is not discussed.

night-watchman-state.rationale: The programme demands a welfare state and public health system.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Schönerer's movement barred members with Jewish relatives or friends, implying disapproval, but marriage is not documented.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: The Aryan paragraph and descent-based antisemitism denied equal standing, although the modern programme affirms equal civil rights.

socialism-one-country.rationale: Socialist strategy is not addressed; adherents are indifferent.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: The programme honours the historical settlement of its own land and ancestry.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: The programme demands that religious communities respect state law and the constitution.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Los-von-Rom urged Germans to convert away from Catholicism, so restricting conversion contradicts its campaign.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: No source touches the matter; the programme rejects religious dogma in lawmaking.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Anti-clerical heritage points to secular schooling, though the programme says nothing directly.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: Socialist state theory is outside the ideology; adherents are indifferent.

consent-of-governed.rationale: The movement used self-determination of peoples as its argument and the programme grounds the state in democracy.

trade-surplus.rationale: The programme celebrates export orientation of industry.

population-transfer.rationale: The programme calls Beneš decrees on the expulsion of Germans a human-rights violation to be repealed.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: The programme endorses force for state security and defence.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Pan-German ethnocentrism saw peoples as rivals, and the programme prizes performance.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Austria banned the Nazi party in 1933 while Third Camp members were later victims and critics of bans, so adherents are split.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: Not discussed in sources; adherents are indifferent to the republican theory.

separated-powers.rationale: The programme explicitly commits to constitutional principles including separation of powers.

vanguard-party.rationale: The programme demands democratic competition and rejects ideological parties leading the state.

priority-to-poor.rationale: The programme says welfare goes first to citizens and performers rather than to the poor as such.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: The programme favours property formation, though social housing is reserved for citizens.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Neither the programme nor the historical sources discuss strike law, and nationalist working-class and Mittelstand wings would pull in opposite directions.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: The programme wants population growth through birth-oriented policy.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: The programme rejects forced multiculturalism and mass immigration, and the German-Austrian concept counts only German-descent Austrians as real Austrians.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: The programme demands elections and direct votes.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: The programme commits to Rechtsstaat and liberal freedoms.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: The programme commits to a market economy with low state intervention, so price fixing is inferred as unwelcome even in scarcity.

party-controls-media.rationale: The programme demands media laws preventing monopolies and manipulation.

party-commands-army.rationale: The programme places the Bundesheer under the sovereign state.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: The programme restricts citizenship to well-integrated, culturally rooted newcomers.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Nothing indicates it; the programme is conventional on parliament.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Schönerer's Führer system was disciplined but the modern programme is silent.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: The programme demands constitutional precedence over EU law and a Europe of sovereign fatherlands.

head-commands-forces.rationale: The programme speaks of the state as a sovereign, republican democracy.

church-by-bishops.rationale: The movement was hostile to Catholic hierarchy and promoted leaving it.

clerical-rule.rationale: The movement fought political Catholicism and launched Away from Rome, so rule by senior clerics is the opposite of its aims.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: National loyalty and the Anschluss goal contradict it.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: The programme says art is limited only by law and demands artistic freedom.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: The programme's constitutional order stresses checks and republican principles.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: The programme demands no military pact membership and home defence priority, though historically the Linz framers backed the alliance with Germany.

recall-officials.rationale: The programme's direct democracy push suggests this.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: The programme supports social housing and market economy.

people-in-arms.rationale: The programme endorses a conscript Bundesheer.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: The programme values the peasantry and natural landscape.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: Pan-Germans demanded German unification across the border imposed by Saint-Germain, and the programme seeks Tirol's unity.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: German-nationalist student fraternities were the movement's base.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Schönerer's ethnic hierarchy and anti-Slav stance deny equal cultural standing.

death-penalty.rationale: The programme states that the death penalty is categorically rejected.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: The programme rejects gender mainstreaming and puts the male-female family at the centre of education values, so curricula on gender equality are inferred as opposed.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: The programme demands free science and no ideological interference, and the movement was anti-clerical.

restrict-pornography.rationale: Protection of children and moral outlook suggest support.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: The German-Austrian concept counts those of German descent and language as the real Austrians.

minority-language-support.rationale: The Linz Program made German the official language, though the modern programme protects autochthonous groups.

religious-exemptions.rationale: The programme insists religious communities obey state law.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: The programme values tradition and community.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: The programme rejects aid beyond self-help and favours budget discipline.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: The programme treats sovereignty as a political and cultural matter within a market economy and never calls for transforming the property system.

constituent-assembly.rationale: German Austria's 1918 order was founded by an assembly; the programme backs direct democracy.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: The programme commits to liberal basic freedoms.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: The programme limits aid to help to self-help and puts Austrian interests first.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: The programme rejects nuclear power and favours neutrality.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: Inferred from the programme's push for direct democracy; it does not discuss how the president is chosen.

central-bank-independence.rationale: The programme demands balanced budgets but never mentions central banks, and EU-sceptic adherents distrust the ECB, so no firm position can be stated.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: The programme claims unity of Tirol and rejects Beneš decrees.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: The programme protects private property while tying science to Gemeinwohl.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: A debate within Marxism that the sources never touch; adherents were anti-communist but have no theory of the question.

precautionary-principle.rationale: The programme values protection of nature and sustainable use.

collective-defense.rationale: The programme demands no military pact membership.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: Adherents fought the Saint-Germain boundaries yet celebrated the 1938 annexation, so the principle splits.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Schönerer fought political Catholicism and the programme limits privileges of religious bodies.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: A republican constitutional order implies a unifying president.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Pan-Germans worked to detach regions from states they were in.

region-keeps-system.rationale: The programme endorses federal and Tyrolean autonomy.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Schönerer was hostile to the Habsburg throne.

flat-income-tax.rationale: The programme wants a socially balanced tax system.

character-from-environment.rationale: Descent-based racial antisemitism implies innate nature shapes character.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: The programme commits to the Rechtsstaat and separation of powers, which excludes a ruler unbound by law.

space-expansion.rationale: Nothing in the sources addresses it, and a programme centred on homeland, tradition and national interests would not make space a civilisational goal.

mixed-constitution.rationale: The sources show no interest in classical constitutional theory, and the programme's republican democracy with referendums does not map onto it.

leader-cult.rationale: Schönerer's followers called him Führer and promoted a Bismarck cult.

equal-parenting.rationale: The programme wants joint parental responsibility to continue after separation.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: Marxist-Leninist theory is alien to the movement, which rejected class struggle in favour of the nation; opposition is inferred.

land-redistribution.rationale: The programme protects property and peasants.

refugee-return.rationale: The programme supports expellee associations and repeal of Beneš decrees.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Anschluss and the demand to represent German-speaking Altösterreicher rest on the nationality principle.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: The programme says freedom of religion includes the freedom to leave dogmas.

women-must-cover.rationale: The programme rejects religious dogma in public order and demands equal treatment.

common-currency.rationale: The programme criticises EU integration and wants a Europe of sovereign fatherlands, so a shared currency is inferred as unwelcome.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Pan-Germanism sought the political union of German-speaking peoples across borders.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: The Linz Program wanted German as official language and unified Austria opposed to Slavic autonomy.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: Schönerer wanted Jews removed from public life, not equal-rights struggle.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: The programme's idealist worldview denies materialism.

ban-cartels.rationale: The programme criticises monopoly-oriented agribusiness and media.

no-bailouts.rationale: The programme wants thrifty use of public funds.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: The programme commits to Rechtsstaat and separation of powers.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: The programme stresses constitutional liberal freedoms.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: The programme explicitly opposes quotas and preferential treatment of one sex to remove disadvantages.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: The programme praises the export orientation of Austrian industry, which a closed autarkic bloc would contradict.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: The sources give no stance on trade-treaty clauses; adherents split between protectionist and free-trade instincts.

moral-incentives.rationale: The programme says honest performance must pay and favours material rewards for effort.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: The programme condemns extremism, though 1930s Nazi cells used force.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: The movement opposed the Habsburg dynastic establishment.

history-own-civilization.rationale: The programme demands schools convey the traditions and values of the community.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Schönerer wanted Czechs Germanised and German dominance in Austria.

patriotic-education.rationale: The programme wants schools to convey values and traditions of the community.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: The programme rejects preferential treatment on group basis.

public-money-creation.rationale: Monetary reform is not part of the programme.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: The programme assumes a durable market economy with social responsibility, implying capitalism can adapt rather than collapse.

former-empire-influence.rationale: The programme advocates for Altösterreicher in former k.u.k. lands.

delink-world-market.rationale: The programme values Austria's technology- and export-oriented industry, which relies on integration with world markets.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: A Marxist-Leninist thesis outside the movement's frame; the nationalist view sees Austrian prosperity as earned by its own people.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: The programme demands equality before law, though Schönerer's association set the Aryan paragraph for itself.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: Adherents rejected Saint-Germain as an imposed partition of the German people.

elective-rulers.rationale: The movement favoured a republic over the Habsburg throne.

minority-veto.rationale: The programme wants majority democracy with proportional elections and referendums, not unanimity rules.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: Inferred from the programme's Rechtsstaat and liberal freedoms and the movement's own opposition to the Habsburg state.

parliament-supreme.rationale: The programme endorses parliamentary democracy and budget discipline.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: The programme says animals as fellow creatures are protected from torment.

animal-use-humane.rationale: The programme speaks of respectful treatment while supporting agriculture.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: The programme speaks of solidarity of compatriots and generations, which implies duties of the better off toward their own community.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: The movement was agitational under Schönerer and the programme calls on citizens to contribute personally to national life.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: The programme criticises media manipulation, but not through critical theory.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: Gramscian hegemony theory is not part of the movement's thinking, which stressed nation and ethnicity over class rule.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: The programme limits aid to help to self-help and does not blame world-economy structure; inferred rejection.

native-born-offices.rationale: The ethnic-German concept of the real Austrian suggests this.

party-own-road.rationale: A dispute internal to communist parties; the movement has no stake in it.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: The programme's aid principle is help to self-help.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Adherents rejected Saint-Germain and the programme seeks Tirol's unity.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: The programme treats historically settled minorities as part of the state people, not as holders of leadership over settlers.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: The post-war Third Camp opposed de-Nazification.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: The programme pledges to defend the free democratic order against fanaticism and extremism generally, though post-war adherents resisted Nazi-only framing.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: An American historiographic dispute never addressed by the movement.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: The programme stresses preservation of cultural monuments.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: The programme rejects favouring either sex to compensate disadvantages, implying equal attention to boys and men.

domestic-violence-symmetry.rationale: The programme demands severe penalties for violence against children and the vulnerable but takes no position on gender symmetry.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: The programme's Europe of peoples stresses own forms.

military-guardian-role.rationale: The programme places the army under democratic state.

paid-care-work.rationale: The programme demands pension credit for care work.

filial-duty.rationale: The programme stresses solidarity of generations.

office-by-exam.rationale: Civil-service recruitment is not discussed, and the movement's democratic and völkisch strands point different ways.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: The programme demands sovereignty and Austria first.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: The programme addresses divorce only regarding children.

recallable-delegates.rationale: The programme endorses representative democracy with referendums.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: The programme wants a harmonised state pension.

land-use-tenure.rationale: The programme protects private property and a free peasantry on owned farms, contrary to community ownership of land.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: Follows from the programme's parliamentary Rechtsstaat and demand for a disciplined, parliament-controlled budget.

single-official-language.rationale: The Linz Program made German the official language and the programme requires German for school.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: Inferred from the Austria-first stance and demand that national prosperity benefit citizens first; not stated in the programme.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: The programme says freedom is not limited to material needs.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: The programme demands neutrality and non-involvement in foreign conflicts beyond peacekeeping.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: The programme insists on national sovereignty and decisions on the use of force by Austria alone.

corporate-influence.rationale: The programme attacks monopolistic agribusiness and media monopolies, implying concern about corporate power over politics.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: Follows from the Austria-first and sovereignty emphasis, though the programme does not mention NGO funding.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: The programme says Austria is not an immigration country and pursues birth-oriented family policy.

residents-only-property.rationale: Inferred from its Austria-first, homeland-protection stance; local property limits are not discussed.

job-guarantee.rationale: The programme favours market economy and low state spending, not a state employer of last resort.

democratic-peace.rationale: The sources show no view on this thesis, and a nationalist outlook neither embraces nor denies it.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: The programme names law and order a basic value and the Rechtsstaat a pillar of freedom.

non-intervention.rationale: The programme demands sovereignty and neutrality.

industrial-unions.rationale: Union structure is not discussed anywhere in the sources.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Schönerer fought Jewish influence over press and finance.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: The programme gives marriage between man and woman a priority position and special protection.

public-access-to-information.rationale: The programme demands media laws against manipulation.

local-production.rationale: The programme values peasants and fair prices.

informal-organisation.rationale: Schönerer's associations were hierarchical with a Führer, so loose informal groups are inferred as foreign to the movement.

national-law-over-international.rationale: The programme gives constitutional principles of member states absolute primacy over Community law.

religious-nation.rationale: The nation is defined by language and descent.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: The programme insists on sovereignty and self-determination, ruling out tributary deference.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: The Linz Program opposed extending federalism.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: The programme protects private property of all kinds.

defeat-communism.rationale: Inferred from the programme's commitment to defend the free order against extremism; not stated against communism in particular.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: The programme wants efficient public health services and low taxes but gives no model for provider mix.

religion-illusion.rationale: The programme values Christianity as culture and heritage, although Schönerer himself left the Catholic Church.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: The programme's endorsement of a market economy and performance suggests it sees capitalism as a force for prosperity.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: The programme sees equality as equal opportunity and fair pay, not transformation of the economic system.

socialized-care.rationale: The programme prefers raising children in family security to state substitutes and supports care by relatives.

purge-loanwords.rationale: The programme wants the mother tongue protected.

treaties-binding.rationale: The programme respects autochthonous minorities but sources are silent on treaty rights of nations within the state.

cooperative-communities.rationale: The programme protects private property and individual enterprise, the opposite of communal property.

majority-settlement.rationale: Schönerer wanted the Germanising of Czech areas.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: The camp called itself neither liberal nor clerical but national.

historical-land-claim.rationale: The programme claims Tirol unity and Altösterreicher interests.

holocaust-denial.rationale: The programme condemns extremism and Austrian law bans denial.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: The programme rejects unions but speaks of human dignity.

suppress-opposition.rationale: The programme explicitly commits to liberal freedoms of opinion, assembly and press and to democracy.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: The programme demands freedom to leave dogma.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Austria had no overseas colonies and the sources never raise the question; inferred from its Austria-first outlook as mild support at most.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: An Islamic doctrine outside the movement; adherents' hostility toward Islam makes agreement unlikely.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: The programme bases politics on constitutional democracy and rejects religious dogma in lawmaking.

participatory-democracy.rationale: The programme's direct-democracy demands imply support for broader participation, though not in workplaces.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: The programme rejects gender mainstreaming and group preferences and sees such frameworks as ideological.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: The programme rejects gender mainstreaming and defines family as man and woman; recognition is inferred as opposed.

assisted-dying.rationale: The programme says life is beyond utility considerations.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: The programme claims no ideological reservations while the camp keeps its position.

alienated-labor.rationale: Marxist theory of alienation is outside the movement, whose programme honours work and performance.

islam-incompatible.rationale: The programme speaks of defending culture against displacing cultures.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: The programme grounds authority in democracy and the free democratic order and affirms church-state separation.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: Inferred from the programme's church-state separation and wariness of religious dogma in public institutions.

ban-nda-harassment.rationale: A workplace-law detail the sources never touch.

social-market-economy.rationale: The programme explicitly commits to a market economy with social responsibility.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: The programme demands best equipment for the Bundesheer.

rich-first.rationale: The programme calls for fair division of contributions and benefits and equal opportunity, not unequal growth.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: The programme demands neutrality and no military pact membership.

dynastic-succession.rationale: The movement opposed the Habsburg dynasty, and the programme is republican.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: The programme endorses market economy and says nothing of mutual banking.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: Inferred from sovereignty and anti-EU-dictate stance, though the programme itself favours sound budgets.

property-franchise.rationale: The programme demands a free, equal and direct vote for all citizens.

domination-women-nature.rationale: An ecofeminist thesis outside the movement, though the programme values nature protection.

reification.rationale: A Marxist-Hegelian concept foreign to the movement and its idealist worldview.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: Schönerer attacked liberal press ties to firms.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: The programme commits to the Rechtsstaat and constitutional principles including separation of powers.

online-participation.rationale: Inferred from the programme's calls for direct democracy and citizen decision-making.

open-government-data.rationale: Inferred from the programme's demands for transparency against manipulation of public opinion; not stated for government records.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: The secular programme and Schönerer's own anti-clericalism oppose religious control of marriage.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: Inferred from Schönerer's antisemitism and demand to remove Jewish influence from public life; shop boycotts are not documented in the sources opened.

citizens-assembly.rationale: Sortition is not discussed, and direct-democracy sympathy is offset by the programme's preference for elections.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: The movement had no theology position beyond anti-clericalism; adherents split.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Schönerer attacked the liberal capitalists around the press and railways, implying worry about concentrated wealth.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: Inferred from the programme's rejection of same-sex partnership and strong military traditionalism.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: The programme defends freedom of religion, even while keeping church and state apart.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: The programme demands strong security forces.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: The Linz Program wanted German dominance and opposed turning Austria into a Slavic state, not consociational sharing.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: The programme affirms the social state, public health and social housing rather than leaving the poor to charity.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: After the 1873 crash Schönerer denounced the liberal establishment and press for corrupt ties to business, and the modern Freedom Party presents itself against an entrenched political class.

racial-franchise.rationale: The movement's ethnic idea of the nation points that way, but the FPÖ programme demands an equal, direct vote for all citizens, and citizenship itself is open to assimilated immigrants.

term-limits.rationale: Inferred: neither Schönerer's movement nor the FPÖ programme takes up term limits, and adherents favour direct-democratic tools rather than limiting tenure.

vote-delegation.rationale: Inferred: the Third Camp stresses referendums and national sovereignty over representation, not revocable delegation of votes, and the Schönerer era distrusted parliamentary mechanics.

existential-risk-priority.rationale: Inferred: the movement's concerns are national identity, borders and sovereignty, and it never addressed extinction risks either way.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: Inferred: Away from Rome pushed conversion to Protestantism and hostility to the Catholic hierarchy, but the strand never took a position on women's clerical eligibility.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: Inferred: the FPÖ programme centres the family of spouses and children without asserting husband headship, and modern Austrian law sets equal partnership, which later adherents accept.

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: The 2011 FPÖ programme prioritises Austrian citizens and restricts immigration and the franchise is tied to citizenship.

rent-control.rationale: Third Camp economic views vary by era (anti-capitalist under Schönerer, mixed since); no settled position.

abolish-ip.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from its stress on property and national economy.

uniformed-youth.rationale: Interwar pan-German bodies were organised and militant but the post-1945 FPÖ does not demand drilled youth movements; eras differ.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: The FPÖ programme stresses neutrality and opposes nuclear power; inferred for weapons.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: The programme stresses sovereignty and neutrality, which cuts against foreign bases; inferred.

recognise-genocide.rationale: The tradition has often minimised or contested guilt narratives; inferred from its history of revisionism.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: Schönerer attacked finance and the FPÖ programme stresses performance and the productive middle class; inferred.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: Early nationalism glorified German heroism and combat, and the modern programme upholds military defence of the homeland.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: The movement holds that Austrians belong to the German Volk and cultural community with continuity from its origins.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: The FPÖ programme opposes gender mainstreaming and stresses natural sex differences; inferred.

no-fixed-category-of-women.rationale: Inferred from the programme's emphasis on the traditional family and rejection of gender ideology.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: Honouring the fallen of the German nation is part of this tradition; not stated in the sources opened.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: Schönerer fought political Catholicism and was not framing politics as a spiritual war; inferred.

homeland-cultural-centre.rationale: Pan-Germanism sought to unite all Germans in one state, not leave them in diaspora centres.

culture-before-state.rationale: Political and territorial union came first for Schönerer and Pan-German parties; inferred.

god-not-male.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the movement's traditionalism and rejection of progressive gender politics.

scripture-judged-by-women.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from its rejection of feminist politics.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: Early Schönerer demands removed Jews from economic and public life; the modern programme only privileges citizens; eras differ.

single-unit-for-people.rationale: Its defining aim is a Greater Germany uniting all German-speaking regions in one territorial unit.

independent-unions.rationale: Third Camp parties claimed to speak for workers but were anti-socialist and eras differ; the sources do not address union independence.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: The movement opposed socialist class politics and put the nation first; inferred.

local-essentials-public.rationale: The FPÖ programme supports public provision of basic services; inferred at low confidence.

second-chamber.rationale: Eras differ: Schönerer attacked parliament, the post-1945 FPÖ accepts the Bundesrat; inferred.

municipal-property.rationale: The movement defended private property and the national community, not municipal ownership; inferred.

confederal-coordination.rationale: Pan-German centralism favours national unity over confederal local rule; inferred.

family-wage.rationale: The 2011 FPÖ programme stresses support for the family; inferred this extends to household income.

faster-drug-approval.rationale: Inferred from the movement's cautious, tradition-minded stance; the sources never discuss drug approval.

ageing-research-funding.rationale: Inferred from the stress on nature, tradition and limiting growth; the sources never discuss it.

anonymous-payments.rationale: Inferred from the pro-surveillance, security-minded stance of the movement.

online-anonymity.rationale: Inferred from the movement's pro-security and identity-focused stance; not discussed.

person-over-state.rationale: The movement puts the Volk community above the individual, as in the Linz Program's national aims.

spiritual-nature.rationale: Eras differ: Schönerer's Away from Rome rejected the church, the 2011 programme invokes Christian-occidental culture.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: Pan-German nationalism favoured centralised national authority; inferred from its opposition to local autonomy.

gm-crops.rationale: The FPÖ has opposed genetically modified food; low confidence as the sources do not discuss it.

dense-cities.rationale: Inferred from the Heimat and rural-tradition emphasis; the sources never discuss it.

racial-group-interests.rationale: Schönerer's Linz Program and 1885 Aryan paragraph put race and descent at the centre of the nation.

racial-pride.rationale: The movement celebrated German descent and the Volk; low confidence because post-1945 versions stress culture over race.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: Eras differ: Schönerer-era pan-Germanism was expansionist, while the post-1945 FPÖ stresses sovereignty and neutrality.

missingStatements.text: The state should exclude members of a particular ethnic or religious group from public office and the professions.
missingStatements.rationale: Schönerer demanded Jews be removed from public life and his 1885 additions to the Linz Program called for ending Jewish influence, so the early movement answered strongly yes, though the modern FPÖ programme does not.
missingStatements.declined: Existing racial-franchise answer is -1 (modern FPÖ-era mainstream) and conflicts with this proposal, which holds only for the early Schönerer movement.

missingStatements.text: Political parties should not be organised on the basis of a church or religion.
missingStatements.rationale: The Away from Rome movement arose against Catholic political parties allied with the Slavs, and Schönerer fought political Catholicism.

notes: The strands differ: Schönerer's racial antisemitism and anti-Habsburg radicalism, interwar pan-Germans absorbed into the NSDAP, and the post-1945 FPÖ that combines German cultural identity with Austrian patriotism and formal democracy. Answers lean on the 2011 FPÖ programme for modern policy positions, so many economic and social answers rest on inference from a party that is only partly this ideology.
